extracted.intended_audience: users of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system (mathematicians, symbolic-computation practitioners, control-theory and PDE/finite-difference researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR libraries (control.lib, jacobson.lib, findifs.lib, etc.), specifying procedure usages, assumptions, return types, and behavioral/algorithmic notes for performing algebraic analysis, control-theory computations, Smith/Jacobson normal forms, and finite-difference scheme generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: decodeRandomFL argument semantics and minimal polynomial requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decodeRandomFL(redun,p,e,n,t,ncodes,ntrials,minpol); - n is length of codes generated, - redun = redundancy of codes generated, - p is the characteristic, - e is the extension degree, - t is the number of errors to correct, - ncodes is the number of random codes to be processed, - ntrials is the number of received vectors per code to be corrected, - minpol: due to some pecularities of SINGULAR one needs to provide minimal polynomial for the extension explicitly
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the minimal polynomial for the field extension explicitly (minpol argument) because of SINGULAR peculiarities; pass parameters in the specified order. Examples in the text show typical binary-code usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: control — compute controllability-related properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: control(R); R a module (R is the matrix of the system of equations to be investigated). Return: list. Purpose: compute the list of all the properties concerning controllability of the system (behavior), represented by the matrix R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure investigates controllability, flatness, dimension of the system, degree of controllability, kernel and image representations, genericity of parameters, obstructions to controllability, annihilator of torsion submodule and left inverse. Use when you need a comprehensive controllability analysis of a system-module.

rubrics_metrics.name: controlDim — dimension-based controllability analysis (full-row-rank requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: controlDim(R); R a module (R is the matrix of the system of equations to be investigated). Return: list. Purpose: computes list of all the properties concerning controllability of the system (behavior) represented by the matrix R. This procedure is analogous to 'control' but uses dimension calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The implemented approach works for full row rank matrices only (the check is done automatically). Use controlDim when you prefer dimension calculations and ensure R has full row rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: autonom — compute autonomy-related properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autonom(R); R a module (R is a matrix of the system of equations which is to be investigated). Return: list. Purpose: find all the properties concerning autonomy of the system (behavior) represented by the matrix R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigates autonomy, strong autonomy, system dimension, autonomy degree, kernel representation and (over)determinacy. Use for analyzing autonomy/observability style properties of system modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: autonomDim — dimension-based autonomy analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: autonomDim(R); R a module. Return: list. Purpose: computes the list of all the properties concerning autonomy of the system (behavior) represented by the matrix R. This procedure is analogous to 'autonom' but uses dimension calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use autonomDim for autonomy analysis based on dimension computations; analogous caveats as controlDim apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: leftKernel — compute left kernel of a matrix/module
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: leftKernel(M); M a matrix. Return: module. Purpose: computes left kernel of matrix M (a module of all elements v such that vM=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a module of generators; examples show checking by printing L*M to obtain zero. Use to compute relations on rows (left nullspace).

rubrics_metrics.name: rightKernel — compute right kernel of a matrix/module
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightKernel(M); M a matrix. Return: module. Purpose: computes the right kernel of matrix M (a module of all elements v such that Mv=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns module generators for nullspace of columns; check via M*R = 0 in examples. Use to obtain column-space relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: leftInverse existence condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: leftInverse(M); M a module. Return: module. Purpose: computes such a matrix L, that LM = Id; Note: exists only in the case when M is free submodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: leftInverse is only defined when the module M is free; examples show trivial and derived examples and verify L*M = 1. Ensure freeness prior to calling.

rubrics_metrics.name: rightInverse existence condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: rightInverse(M); M a module. Return: module. Purpose: computes such a matrix L, that ML = Id; Note: exists only in the case when M is free submodule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: rightInverse requires M to be a free submodule. Examples demonstrate construction and verification via M*L = 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: colrank computation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: colrank(M); M a matrix/module. Return: int. Purpose: compute the column rank of M as of matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedure uses the Bareiss algorithm. Example shows usage on a de Rham complex matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: genericity — parametric non-zero assumptions and recommended options
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: genericity(M); M is a matrix/module. Return: list (of strings). Purpose: determine parametric expressions which have been assumed to be non-zero in the process of computing the Groebner basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The output list consists of strings; the first string contains variables only, further strings contain single polynomials in parameters. Strong recommendation: switch on the redSB and redTail options. The procedure is effective with the lift procedure for modules with parameters. Use to learn which parameter combinations were assumed nonzero during Groebner computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: canonize — canonical reduced minimal Groebner bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: canonize(L); L a list. Return: list. Purpose: modules in the list are canonized by computing their reduced minimal (= unique up to constant factor w.r.t. the given ordering) Groebner bases. Assume: L is the output of control/autonomy procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use canonize to obtain uniquely determined module presentations (up to constants) from control/autonomy outputs; examples show the canonicalized presentation and obstructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: iostruct — compute input-output representation (uses Bareiss)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: iostruct(R); R a module. Return: list L with entries: string s, intvec v, module P and module Q. Purpose: if R is the kernel-representation-matrix of some system, then we output an input-output representation Py=Qu of the system, the components that have been chosen as outputs (intvec v) and a comment s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedure uses the Bareiss algorithm. Use to derive explicit input-output form and chosen outputs from a kernel representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: findTorsion — compute submodule annihilated by ideal I
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: findTorsion(R, I); R an ideal/matrix/module, I an ideal. Return: module. Purpose: computes the Groebner basis of the submodule of R, annihilated by I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially helpful when I is the annihilator of the t(R) - the torsion submodule of R. In this case, the result is the explicit presentation of t(R) as the submodule of R. Examples illustrate extraction of torsion generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: controlExample — setup and use examples from mini-database
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: controlExample(s); s a string. Return: ring. Purpose: set up an example from the mini database by initalizing a ring and a module in a ring. Note: to see list of examples call controlExample("show"); to use an example do def A = controlExample("Antenna"); setring A;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlExample("show") to list available example names/descriptions. After def’ing the example result and setring, you can call control(R) or autonom(R) directly on the pre-defined example module.

rubrics_metrics.name: view — formatted output utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: view(M); M is of any type. Return: no return value. Purpose: procedure for (well-) formatted output of modules, matrices, lists of modules, matrices; shows everything even if entries are long. Note: in case of other types (not 'module','matrix','list') works just as standard 'print' procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use view to get readable formatted display of large entries (matrices, ideals, lists). Examples show use on matrices and composed lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: smith — Smith Normal Form assumptions and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: smith(M[, eng1, eng2]); M matrix, eng1 and eng2 are optional integers. Return: matrix or list of matrices, depending on arguments. Assume: Basering is a commutative polynomial ring in one variable. Purpose: compute the Smith Normal Form of M with (optionally) transformation matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default returns Smith form only. If eng1 non-zero returns {U,D,V} with U*M*V = D. Optional eng2 selects Groebner engine: 0 uses 'slimgb' (default), otherwise 'std'. Use divideUnits to normalize diagonal entries. Use printlevel to control debug/progress messages (printlevel=1 prints progress, >=2 prints all debug messages).

rubrics_metrics.name: jacobson — Jacobson normal form assumptions and options
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jacobson(M, eng); M matrix, eng an optional int. Return: list. Assume: Basering is a (non-commutative) ring in two variables. Purpose: compute a weak Jacobson normal form of M over the basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns list L = {U,D,V} with L[1]*M*L[3] = L[2] diagonal. Optional eng2 selects Groebner engine (0->'slimgb' default, otherwise 'std'). Use printlevel to control debug output. Note: strong Jacobson form may or may not exist depending on algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: divideUnits — postprocess smith/jacobson outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: divideUnits(L); list L. Return: matrix or list of matrices. Assume: L is an output of smith or jacobson procedures (diagonal matrix or list {U,D,V}). Purpose: divide out units from the diagonal and reflect this in transformation matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use divideUnits to normalize diagonal entries (remove unit factors) and update U and V accordingly; examples show two-pendula normalization producing normalized Smith form and modified transformation matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: findifs overall method — finite-difference scheme generation via Groebner bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview: provide presentation of difference operators in polynomial, semi-factorized and nodal form. The computation of a finite difference scheme of a given single linear PDE with constant coefficients and given approximation rules boils down to the computation of a Groebner basis of a submodule of a free module with respect to the ordering eliminating module components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Running findifs_example() demonstrates how to generate schemes. The approach requires setting up the ring, matrix of equations and approximations, using module/std elimination and extracting the scheme polynomial from the resulting Groebner basis output.

rubrics_metrics.name: decoef — decompose polynomial by parameter presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: decoef(P,n); P a poly, n a number. Return: ideal. Purpose: decompose polynomial P into summands with respect to the presence of the number n in the coefficients. Note: n is usually a parameter with no power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decoef to split polynomial into parts depending on a parameter (e.g., dt) to prepare for nodal/form conversion or factorization steps. Examples illustrate decomposition results.

rubrics_metrics.name: difpoly2tex — convert difference polynomial to nodal TeX form (preconditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: difpoly2tex(S,P[,Q]); S an ideal, P and optional Q are lists. Return: string. Purpose: present the difference scheme in the nodal form. Assume: ideal S is the result of decoef procedure; a list P may be empty or contain parameters that will not appear in denominators; optional list Q represents part depending on other functions than the major part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure S is output of decoef; supply P to mark parameters that should not appear in denominators; optional Q can append other-function-dependent parts. Examples show TeX nodal output and use of additional optional args.

rubrics_metrics.name: exp2pt — convert polynomial to TeX nodal form (coefficients constraint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: exp2pt(P[,L]); P poly, L an optional list of strings. Return: string. Purpose: convert a polynomial M into the TeX format, in nodal form. Assume: coefficients must not be fractional. Note: optional list L contains a string to replace default 'u' name for discretized function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not call on polynomials with fractional coefficients unless preprocessing; use optional argument to change variable name in TeX output. Examples show replacing 'u' with 'F'.

rubrics_metrics.name: texcoef — TeX-formatting of numbers/polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: texcoef(n); n a number. Return: string. Purpose: converts the number n into TeX format. Note: if n is a polynomial, texcoef adds extra brackets and performs some space substitutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to transform numeric or polynomial coefficients into TeX-ready strings; examples show conversions like dt/(4*dh^2-dt) -> \frac{\tri t}{4\tri h^{2}-\tri t}.

rubrics_metrics.name: npar — parameter index lookup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: npar(n); n a number. Return: int. Purpose: searches for 'n' among the parameters and returns its number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns 0 and prints 'Incorrect parameter' if the argument is not an exact parameter (e.g., dh^2 is rejected). Use to query parameter ordering in a ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: magnitude — square magnitude of complex expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: magnitude(P); P a poly. Return: poly. Purpose: compute the square of the magnitude of a complex expression. Assume: i is the variable of a basering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes i is the imaginary unit variable with relation i^2+1 (examples use std(i^2+1) for normalization). Useful for simplifying expressions with complex parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: replace / xchange — string manipulation utilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: replace(s,what,with); xchange(w,a,b). Return: string. Purpose: replace in 's' all substrings 'what' with 'with' (replace) or exchange substring 'a' with substring 'b' in string w (xchange).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to post-process TeX/text strings (e.g., rename Tt->T_t, dt->\tri t, replace parameter names with LaTeX commands). Examples show sequential replacements to build TeX-ready strings.
